newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU cuts flour export refund to eight Ecus.
newsitem.headline: EU cuts flour export refund to eight Ecus.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday cut its main wheat flour export refund to eight Ecus per tonne, just a day after cutting it to 10 Ecus to stave off speculation.
French cereals office ONIC said the decision to reduce the refund further was taken at weekly grain talks in Brussels.
The EU on Wednesday cut the refund to 10 Ecus from 17 Ecus in what an EU official described as an effort to prevent speculation caused by a sharp fall in underlying wheat refunds.
The flour refund is now well below the maximum wheat grain refund of 10.25 Ecus per tonne awarded at Thursday's EU tender.
The EU traditionally sets its wheat flour export refund at a margin 1.37 times higher than its highest wheat export subsidy.
But EU officials were concerned about a possible run on flour export licences after the value of wheat refunds traded on the open market plunged earlier this week.

One official said the Commission had used its discretionary powers to reject bids for 140,000 tonnes of wheat flour exports through its daily bidding channel this week. The bids were valued at the previous refund level of 17 Ecus per tonne.
The flour refund applies to the main class of soft wheat flour export licences through the daily "common right" system.
